1. Lilly has two independent marketed molecules (tirzepatide in T2D and

3. Manufacturing depth is becoming a genuine scaling moat: additional
   $4.5B Indiana commitment in May 2026 [Actual, Bloomberg/Lilly]. Novo
   has had supply constraints; Lilly is converting capacity into share.
These justify moderate deviation from base rates, but not an unbounded one.

SECTION 2 — BUSINESS QUALITY (Buffett + Lynch)
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 2-1. Business understanding (3 sentences)
LLY is a global patented-pharmaceutical manufacturer whose current financial
performance is dominated by tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro (type 2 diabetes)
and Zepbound (obesity/overweight). It has now added an FDA-approved oral
small-molecule GLP-1, Foundayo (orforglipron), and is preparing to file
retatrutide, a triple-agonist injectable, in Q1 2027. The company also has
franchises in oncology, immunology, neuroscience and genetic medicines,
but near-term earnings are overwhelmingly a GLP-1 class story.
Understandability: High for the revenue driver; Medium for pipeline
probabilities. Not a black box.

Step 2-2. Moat score [Estimate]
- Intangible assets (patents, brands, clinical data): 3/3
- Switching costs: 2/3 (physician/patient inertia moderate; oral switch
  easier)
- Network effects: 1/3 (clinical ecosystem, physician education, scale
  of real-world data)
- Cost advantage: 2/3 (tirzepatide manufacturing at scale, but competitor
  costs also falling)
- Economies of scale: 3/3 (huge dedicated GLP-1 manufacturing)
- Regulatory barriers: 3/3 (FDA approval, supply oversight, Medicare
  rules)
- Data moat: 1/3 (real-world evidence, but not a classic data network)
Total: 15/21 = WIDE moat [Estimate].
Moat direction: Stable to widening near-term (retatrutide/foundayo add
molecules, manufacturing scale increases), but with negative longer-term
signals: Medicare negotiation, Novo oral presence, net-price declines.

Step 2-3. Lynch classification
Fast Grower — with a caveat that the "fast" part is concentrated in one
therapeutic class. Large-cap pharma with 30%+ net margins and 25%+ revenue
growth is rare. The key checks are: hold period limited by patent cliff;
monitor pipeline continuity; avoid paying growth-multiple prices for a
molecule that will one day face generic/small-molecule competition.

  filed data].

  15x [Estimate].
- Capital spending is enormous: FY2025 capex/revenue 12.0% (pack) or
  16.6% (vendor).
Scorecard judgement: Excellent on margins, Good on balance sheet, Adequate

needs are heavy.

   3 years, but SBC is still ~0.6B/yr [Filed].

3. Capex efficiency: 2/3. Dedicated GLP-1 capacity is a constraint-relief
   moat, but incremental ROIC on $10B+ annual capex is unproven.
4. Rationality of reinvestment vs shareholder return: 2/3.

Insider adjustment: 0 (no confirmed insider buying data).
Total capital-allocation score: 10/15 = Good.

SECTION 2.5 — INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Step 2.5-1. R&D capitalisation [Estimate/Assumption]
R&D is not filed in the pack. Using the Q2 2026 release, R&D was 17% of
revenue. For FY2025, estimating R&D ≈ $11–12B [Estimate].
Capitalising 100% of R&D and amortising over 4-5 years would raise
adjusted operating income and adjusted invested capital. However, since a
large part of current R&D supports next-generation obesity / genetic
medicine optionality, the adjusted ROIC is materially higher than GAAP
ROIC.
- GAAP net-income-based return on invested capital (FY2025):
  Net income $20.64B; invested capital = total debt $42.5B + equity
  $26.5B − cash $7.3B ≈ $61.7B → ~33% [Arithmetic/Assumption].
- Capitalising cumulative R&D of roughly $35–40B would push adjusted
  invested capital to ~$100B; adjusted operating income after R&D
  amortisation could rise to ~$25–27B; adjusted ROIC ≈ 25–30%.
  So adjusted ROIC remains well above any plausible WACC (~8%).

Step 2.5-2. SBC treatment [Estimate/Actual]
FY2025 SBC $0.626B [Filed]. Adjusting owner FCF by subtracting SBC
reduces FCF meaningfully only at the margin; we include it in the cash-
flow framework via the OCF/NI ratio (SBC is already deducted in GAAP net
income).

Step 2.5-3. Lease capitalisation [Estimate]
FY2025 operating leases $1.362B [Filed]. Present value of operating-lease
obligations likely $10–14B using a 6–8% discount rate [Estimate]. Adding
to net debt would raise net debt from ~$35B to ~$45–49B, still modest
versus $1,082B market cap.

Step 2.5-4. Brand/data assets
Brand value of tirzepatide/Zepbound is large, but Interbrand-style values
are highly pro-cyclical. I do not add a separate brand asset to the DCF
because the cash-flow model already captures the pricing power.

Step 2.5-5. Owner earnings (Buffett-style, FY2025)
Owner Earnings ≈ Net income + D&A − maintenance capex − Δworking capital.
Maintenance capex for patented-drug manufacturing is probably 40–60% of
total capex [Assumption]. Taking mid-point 50%:
Owner Earnings ≈ $20.640B + $1.997B − $5.4B − (large working capital
build in 2025) ≈ $14–16B [Estimate].
This is why GAAP EPS overstates distributable cash at the current
manufacturing build-out phase.

Discount-rate derivation and terminal
